title: 👑 Elite Challenge ⭐⭐⭐⭐: Master of the Healthy Day

questions.prompt: Three of these sentences are correct English. Which one is NOT correct?

options.text: You should drink water after the match.
You must wash your hands before you eat.
You can swims very fast.
You mustn't eat that, it is bad for you.

questions.explanation: The faulty sentence is the one with swims: after can the verb stays bare, so it must be You can swim very fast. The three other sentences keep their verb bare after should, must and mustn't, which is why they are all correct.

questions.prompt: Which of these sentences gives advice, and leaves the other person free to say no?

options.text: You must take your medicine at eight.
You mustn't touch the hot pan.
You must wear a helmet on a bike.
You should eat a fruit at break time.

questions.explanation: Only should carries a good idea that the other person is still free to follow or not: You should eat a fruit at break time. The three other sentences use must and mustn't, which state something necessary or forbidden, and those leave no choice.

questions.prompt: Read: "Nadia has a headache and she is tired, but she wants to study tonight." Which answer is the best advice, in correct English?

options.text: You must study tonight.
You should to rest tonight.
You should rest tonight.
You shouldn't rest tonight.

questions.explanation: Two things must be right at the same time here. A girl with a headache needs rest, so the good idea is opened by should, not by shouldn't; and after should the verb stays bare, so it is rest and never to rest. The sentence with must turns a piece of advice into a rule, which is not what a tired friend needs.

questions.prompt: Which list contains only nouns that go with the question word How much?

options.text: milk, oil, rice
eggs, milk, rice
biscuits, tomatoes, apples
cheese, biscuits, water

questions.explanation: Milk, oil and rice cannot be counted one by one and none of them takes a plural -s, so all three go with How much. Every other list hides a countable noun that would need How many: eggs, biscuits, tomatoes and apples are all counted one by one.

questions.prompt: Read: "Amine plays football every day, but he is afraid of the water." Which sentence about Amine is completely correct?

options.text: He cans play football but he can't swim.
He can play football and he can swim.
He can't play football but he can swim.
He can play football but he can't swim.

questions.explanation: Amine plays every day, so he is able to play football and the word is can; he is afraid of the water, so he is not able to swim and the word is can't. The sentence with cans puts an -s on a word that never takes one, and the two others exchange his two abilities.

questions.prompt: Which sentence about an ailment and its advice is completely correct?

options.text: I am a stomachache, so I should to eat less.
I have a stomachache, so I should eat less.
I have a stomachache, so I shoulds eat less.
I am a stomachache, so I should eat less.

questions.explanation: An ailment is a noun, so it takes have and not the verb to be, and after should the verb stays bare and should never adds an -s. Only one sentence respects both rules at once: I have a stomachache, so I should eat less.
